body: - Deviation from G-Py-11 (Give every lint or type suppression an inline reason and the narrowest scope that works). The new test file added by this change, `python/tests/report/test_markdown_block.py`, introduces several bare suppressions with no reason text:
- the parametrized table runner: `run_fn(target, block)  # type: ignore[operator]`
- the delegation spy: `recorded.append(kwargs["markers"])  # type: ignore[index]` and `run_fn(target, "NEW\n")  # type: ignore[operator]`

- G-Py-11 prescribes the `# type: ignore[code]  # reason` / `# pyright: ignore[code]  # reason` form and notes the codebase annotates suppressions densely so a bare one reads as unexplained debt; the deviation clause offers no carve-out for bare per-line suppressions in tests. Each of these has an obvious, statable reason (intentional access to a private wrapper to exercise the public delegation contract; calling an `object`-typed callable held in the `CALLERS` table), so a one-phrase reason should be appended to each line.

- The rest of the change is clean: it sweeps both sibling callers of the shared machinery (consistent with the consumer-sweep expectations), routes the file write through `larch.io.atomic_write` rather than re-implementing bare tmp+replace, models the marker pair as a `@dataclass(frozen=True)`, fails loudly via `ValueError` on empty or equal markers, and carries a documented reason on both the new `markdown_block.py` per-file ruff ignore in `python/ruff.toml` and every added `complexity-baseline.json` row.
